ruling.recommended_action: Refund $3.64 to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) for the unexempted F4 detour; note the RD-1 breach on file for the driver and open an account review referral upon execution.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a metered RydeTAXI ride (charged $44.69, F8), so mileage enters the fare and RD-2's per-km formula applies [F8][RD-2]. Two off-route segments are recorded: F3 (17:04–17:11, +2.44 km) and F4 (17:18–17:23, +2.58 km) [F3][F4][RD-1].

F3 is excused by RD-5: the driver asked at 17:01 whether he could "go round via Bedok North Road" [F9] and the rider answered "Sure, your call." at 17:02 [F10], a rider message sent before the 17:04 segment start, and F11 confirms the chat record of two timestamped messages is complete [F11]. The rider's broad "your call" is a general route choice covering the route driven to get round the jam, so F3 is exempt [F10][F11][RD-5]; no RD-3 stop was measured in that segment [RD-3].

F4 is not excused: the only rider message on the record is F10 at 17:02, well before F4 started at 17:18, and F11 shows no later rider message, so no rider agreement covers that stretch [F10][F11][F4][RD-5]. The driver's own post-trip statement F12 ("the second turn-off was my GPS rerouting") is not rider consent and concedes the segment was his own GPS reroute [F12][RD-5]. No reasonable cause applies: F15 records no traffic incident anywhere near the route and F13/F14 show only speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on PIE and CTE, which is above RD-4(b)'s band 1–2 and, standing alone, does not exempt [F13][F14][F15][RD-4]; weather was fair [F16]. F4 is therefore an unexempted detour under RD-1 and refundable under RD-2 [F4][RD-1][RD-2].

Amount: the trip's own rate is the distance fare over distance km, $30.54 ÷ 21.66 km = $1.4100/km [F5][F8][RD-2]. Only the unexempted segment's extra km are refunded: 2.58 km × $1.4100/km = $3.6382, rounded to $3.64 [F4][F5][RD-2]. The remaining billed excess (F5's $7.56 for 5.36 km, i.e. the unmatched balance and the exempt F3 mileage) stays with the fare, as does the $0.13 waiting charge, which is a metered waiting unit on a RydeTAXI trip and is not refundable under RD-3(c) [F5][F6][F8][RD-2][RD-3].

The case is established against the driver (a non-exempt segment and an RD-1 breach) and the profile shows 2 upheld route disputes in 90 days, so this makes the conduct repeated within the RD-6 window: the account review flag is required, and the profile fact is used only for that additional action, never to establish the detour itself [F18][RD-6]. The safety screen read F9, F10 and F12 in context — a route request, a one-line assent and a factual post-trip explanation — and found no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation [F9][F10][F12][SAFE-1].

No RD-4 incident and no band 1–2 congestion exist, so the segment is an unexempted detour refundable under RD-2 [RD-1][RD-4][RD-5][RD-2].

Accepted as to F3 only: F10 does exempt F3 [F9][F10][F11][RD-5], but the same agreement cannot extend to the later F4 segment for which no rider message exists [F4][F11][RD-5]; the citation to RD-3 adds nothing as no rider-named stop was measured [RD-3].

Rejected: F13 and F14 are only speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on PIE and CTE, above RD-4(b)'s band 1–2, and F15 records no incident near the route, so no reasonable-cause exemption covers F4 [F13][F14][F15][RD-4].

Accepted on the flag but rejected as to its sole basis: the profile records 2 upheld route disputes in 90 days [F18], which combines with the breach established in this case to make the conduct repeated [RD-6]; the profile alone could not have decided the case [F18][F4][RD-6].
